items.name: Fresh turkey
items.note: Billy's recipe is written for 12–14 lb. This size feeds 10 with leftovers. If frozen, start thawing 4 days ahead.

items.name: Medium carrots
items.note: Roasted whole. Pick slim ones of a similar size so they cook evenly. Tops trimmed, or a short bit of stem left on for looks.

items.note: Spinach salad.

items.note: Vinaigrette.

items.name: Lemons

items.name: Flat-leaf parsley
items.note: Herb butter, cavity sprigs, stuffing garnish.

items.name: Fresh thyme

items.name: Fresh rosemary

items.name: Unsalted butter
items.note: About 9½ sticks go into recipes: herb butter 4, yams 2¼, rolls 1½, stuffing 1, potatoes ¾. The rest covers green beans, the table and an optional 1–2 tbsp in the gravy.

items.name: Fresh loaf of bread

items.note: Rolls ¼ cup, cranberry sauce 1¼ cups.

items.note: Candied yams at 1.5×.

items.note: Vinaigrette.

items.note: Vinaigrette.

items.name: Cornstarch

items.name: Ground cinnamon

items.name: Parchment paper

items.name: Sheet pans

items.text: Order the turkey, 15–16 lb
items.note: Fresh from a butcher, or a store pre-order.

items.text: Test-fit the oven
items.note: Roasting pan on the bottom rack with a second rack above it. Check that a 13×9 dish and two sheet pans fit. This decides how much can share the oven with the turkey.

items.text: Bake a test batch of the rolls (optional)
items.note: One batch makes 14–16. Freeze a few to try the freezer route.

items.text: Plan fridge space
items.note: A 15–16 lb turkey needs a full shelf, plus room for stuffing, yams and rolls.

items.text: Buy pantry items and equipment
items.note: Flour, sugars, yeast, stock, spices, foil, parchment, twine.

items.text: Buy the bread loaf for stuffing
Charge the Bluetooth thermometer and check the probe
Frozen turkey only: move it to the fridge
items.note: Allow 24 hours per 5 lb, so about 3 days for 15–16 lb. Keep it on a tray on the bottom shelf.

items.text: Buy produce, butter, milk and eggs
Buy fresh herbs
Pick up the fresh turkey
Make the cranberry sauce
items.note: Boil 1 cup water with 1¼ cups sugar, add the cranberries, return to a boil, then cover and simmer about 15 minutes until very thick. Off the heat, stir in cinnamon, nutmeg and orange zest and press the berries to break them up. Use a high-sided pot (they splatter). Keeps 7 days in the fridge.

items.text: Dry the bread cubes
items.note: 300°F for 25–30 minutes until firm. Cool, then store airtight.

items.text: Make and bake the rolls, two separate batches
items.note: Dough rises 1–2 hours, shaped rolls about 1 hour, then 20–25 minutes at 350°F on a lower rack. Cover tightly. They keep 2–3 days at room temperature. Reheat covered at 300°F for about 10 minutes.

items.text: Simmer the neck and giblets for the gravy
items.note: From the turkey cavity. Bring to a boil in water, simmer about 1 hour. Keep the liquid. Pick the neck meat, dice it with the heart and gizzard (discard the liver), and refrigerate both.

items.text: Prep vegetables
items.note: Peel and trim the carrots (leave them whole). Chop onions and celery for the stuffing.

items.text: Make the vinaigrette and toast the pecans
items.note: Shake in a jar: ½ cup olive oil, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1 minced small shallot, ½ tsp salt, pepper. Refrigerate. Toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, then cool and store airtight.

items.text: Trim and blanch the green beans
items.note: Boil in well-salted water for 2–3 minutes, then plunge into ice water. Dry well and refrigerate in a towel-lined container.

items.text: Lay out dishes, pans, serving bowls and utensils
Set the table
Stuffing: brown the sausage, sauté the vegetables, mix with bread, herbs, stock and eggs
items.note: Add the stock slowly. Stop when the bread is moist but not soggy.

items.text: Stuffing into the oven at 350°F
items.note: Covered for 25 minutes, then uncovered for about 20.

items.text: Yams into the oven
items.note: Shortcut from Billy's page: slice, boil 4–6 minutes, drain, coat in the butter and sugar mix, bake at 375°F for 25–30 minutes. Check they are tender.

items.text: Roast the whole carrots at 425°F
items.note: Toss with 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp salt and pepper. One layer on a parchment-lined sheet pan with space between them. 25–30 minutes, turning once, until browned and just tender with a little bite left. They finish cooking in the reheat.

items.text: Cool the stuffing, yams and carrots for 30 minutes, cover, and move to the fridge
items.note: They are reheated from cold later.

items.text: Whip the herb butter
items.note: 5–7 minutes in the stand mixer, then mix in herbs, garlic, salt and pepper.

items.text: Prep the turkey
items.note: Pat dry. Stuff the cavity with lemon, parsley and bay leaves. Butter under the skin on the breast and back. Truss.

items.text: Oven to 450°F
Turkey in: bottom rack, breast up, 450°F for 22–25 minutes
items.note: Until browned on top.

items.text: Flip the turkey breast down, cover the top with bacon, oven to 350°F
items.note: Very hot. Gloves, towels and a second person.

items.text: Remove the bacon and return the turkey to the oven
Start watching the thermometer
items.note: 9–11 minutes per lb after the flip puts the finish at roughly 3:55–4:35. Pull at 165°F in the thickest part.

items.text: Turkey out. Rest on the board, loosely covered in foil
items.note: Billy rests it 15–20 minutes. Wrapped fully in foil or in a cooler it holds up to 90 minutes.

items.text: Reheat stuffing (splash of stock) and yams, covered, at 350°F for about 20 minutes. Glaze the carrots and put them in uncovered
items.note: Carrot glaze: melt 2 tbsp butter with 2 tbsp honey and 1 tbsp chopped thyme, toss with the carrots on their pan. Short on oven room? Warm them in the air fryer at 350°F for 6–8 minutes instead.

items.text: Gravy: pour the pan drippings into the fat separator and skim most of the fat
items.note: Whisk 1 cup drippings with ½ cup flour over medium heat until golden. Add 4 cups stock and 1 more cup drippings, whisk 5–8 minutes until thick, then stir in the giblets. Thin with giblet liquid. Taste before salting, since the bacon makes the drippings salty. Keep warm on low.

items.text: Potatoes: boil 10 minutes, drain, air-dry 10 minutes, shake at the 5-minute mark
Casseroles out, keep covered. Oven to 450°F (475°F without fan)
Potatoes on two sheet pans with oil and spices, into the oven
items.note: Space them an inch apart. 20 minutes, flip, 20 more.

items.text: Carve the turkey
items.note: A job for your helper.

items.text: Flip the potatoes
Sauté the green beans in two batches
items.note: Large skillet, medium-high, 1 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter per batch, 4–5 minutes. Add half the sliced garlic for the last minute. Finish with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice, salt and pepper.

items.text: Warm the rolls
items.note: Air fryer on low for a few minutes, checking often.

items.text: Assemble the spinach salad
items.note: Take the vinaigrette out of the fridge at 5:00 and shake it. Slice the pears now, not earlier, so they don't brown. Toss the spinach with about two-thirds of the dressing, then top with pears, pomegranate, pecans and shaved Parmesan. Extra dressing on the side. A good job for a helper.

items.text: Potatoes out, drizzle with melted butter
Gravy, cranberry sauce and everything to the table
Sit down

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 15–16 lb (recipe is for 12–14 lb)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: 450°F for 22–25 min, flip, 350°F for 9–11 min per lb. Done at 165°F.

lines.label: Notes
lines.text: Herb butter under the skin, bacon on top. Rests 15–20 min, holds up to 90.

recipe.title: The juiciest roast turkey
recipe.time: Prep 30 min · roast about 2½–3¼ hr · rest 20 min

ingredients.name: fresh turkey
ingredients.note: 15–16 lb, neck and giblets removed for the gravy

steps.t: Whip {butter} butter in a stand mixer for 5 to 7 minutes, until light and fluffy.

steps: Mix in {parsley} parsley, {thyme} thyme, {rosemary} rosemary, {sage} sage, {garlic} garlic cloves, {salt} sea salt and {pepper} black pepper.

steps.t: Pat {turkey} turkey completely dry with paper towels, inside and out.

steps: Stuff the cavity with {lemon} halved lemon, a handful of parsley sprigs and {bay} bay leaves.
Gently loosen the skin over the breast and the back with your fingers. Spread the herb butter evenly underneath the skin. Close any tears with toothpicks.
Truss the legs and wings with butcher's twine.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the bottom position.
Set the turkey breast side up on the rack in the roasting pan. Roast 22 to 25 minutes, until browned on top.
Carefully flip the turkey breast side down. It is very hot, so use gloves, towels and a helper. Lay {bacon} bacon strips over the top and lower the oven to 350°F.
Remove the bacon so the back can brown, and keep roasting.
Roast 9 to 11 minutes per pound in total after the flip, about 2¼ to 3 hours for this size. Pull it when the thickest part of the breast or thigh reads 165°F.
Rest loosely covered with foil for 15 to 20 minutes. Wrapped fully in foil or in a cooler it holds up to 90 minutes.

steps: Remove the twine, the toothpicks and the cavity aromatics, then carve.
notes: Billy's recipe is written for a 12–14 lb bird. The herb butter stays the same for 15–16 lb; only the roasting time grows.
Roast on the bottom rack so heat circulates and the bottom doesn't steam.
Frozen turkey: thaw in the fridge, 24 hours per 5 lb.
Leftovers keep 5 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Reheat covered at 350°F with ½–1 cup stock for 15–20 minutes.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: One batch (recipe serves 16), made without the mushrooms

lines.label: Method
lines.text: 350°F, 25 min covered, about 20 uncovered

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Keeps 4 days. Reheat at 350°F for 15–20 min with ¼–⅓ cup stock.

recipe.title: Traditional stuffing

ingredients.name: fresh bread
ingredients.note: cut in cubes, about a 1½ lb loaf

steps.t: Heat the oven to 300°F. Spread {bread} bread cubes on a parchment-lined sheet pan and dry for 25 to 30 minutes, until crisp and firm. Cool, then store airtight.
Melt {butter:1/2} butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown {sausage} sausage, breaking it up, until cooked through. Lift it out of the pan.

steps: Melt {butter:rest} butter in the same pan and cook {onion} onions for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add {celery} celery stalks and {garlic} garlic cloves and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the celery is tender.
Put the vegetables, sausage and dried bread cubes in a large bowl.
Gently mix in {sage} sage, {rosemary} rosemary, {thyme} thyme, and salt and pepper.
Pour in {stock} chicken stock a little at a time, mixing gently. Stop once the bread is moist but not soggy.
Stir in {eggs} whisked eggs.
Spread in a 13×9-inch baking dish and cover with foil.

steps.t: Bake at 350°F for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake about 20 minutes more, until lightly browned on top.
Cool 30 minutes, cover and refrigerate until the reheat.
Reheat covered at 350°F with a splash of stock for about 20 minutes. Garnish with chopped parsley.

notes: Made without the 2 cups of cremini mushrooms in Billy's recipe, so the mushroom step is left out.
Taste the mixture before the eggs go in and adjust the seasoning.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: One batch (recipe serves 15)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Pan drippings roux (1 cup drippings, ½ cup flour), 4 cups stock plus 1 more cup drippings, diced giblets. About 15 minutes while the turkey rests.

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Simmer the neck and giblets the day before. Short on drippings? Top up with 1–2 tbsp butter and a little stock.

recipe.title: Turkey gravy
recipe.time: Giblets 1 hr the day before · gravy 20 min

ingredients.name: turkey neck, heart and gizzard
ingredients.note: from the turkey; discard the liver

steps.t: Put the neck, heart and gizzard in a pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then simmer about 1 hour.

steps: Strain, keeping the liquid. Pick the meat off the neck and dice it with the heart and gizzard. Refrigerate the meat and the liquid separately.

steps.t: Pour the pan drippings into a fat separator or a large bowl. Let the fat rise and skim most of it off.

steps: In a saucepan over medium heat, whisk {drippings:1/2} drippings with {flour} flour into a smooth paste. If it looks greasy, add a little more flour. Cook, whisking, until golden brown.
Whisk in {stock} chicken stock and {drippings:rest} drippings. Keep whisking 5 to 8 minutes, until thickened.
Stir in the diced giblet meat.
Too thick? Thin it with the giblet liquid. Too thin? Simmer 10 minutes more, then whisk in {corn} cornstarch mixed with {water} cold water.
Taste first, then season with salt and pepper. The bacon makes the drippings salty. Keep warm on low until 5:55.
notes: Short on drippings? Top up with 1–2 tbsp butter and a little more stock.
Leftovers keep 2–3 days. Reheat with a splash of stock over medium-low for about 15 minutes.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 1.5× (recipe serves 8)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: 375°F. Boil-first shortcut is 25–30 min; the standard method is 90 min.

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Keeps 5 days. Reheat at 350°F for 15–20 min. Does not freeze well.

recipe.title: Candied yams
recipe.time: Prep 10 min · boil 5 min · bake 25–30 min

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.unmeasured: a pinch, plus some for the water

steps.t: Heat the oven to 375°F.

steps: Boil {yams} sliced yams in salted water for 4 to 6 minutes. Drain well and put them in a large bowl.
In a medium pan over low heat, melt {butter} butter with {sugar} brown sugar, {vanilla} vanilla, {cinnamon} cinnamon, {nutmeg} nutmeg and a pinch of salt. Whisk until smooth.
Pour the warm mixture over the yams and toss until evenly coated.
Spread in a 13×9-inch baking dish and cover with foil. This much is a lot for one dish, so use a deep one or split it.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until very tender.

steps.t: Cool 30 minutes, cover and refrigerate until the reheat.
Reheat covered at 350°F for about 20 minutes.

notes: This uses the boil-first shortcut from Billy's article. His recipe card bakes the raw slices instead: 45 minutes covered, stir, then 45 minutes uncovered.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Does not freeze well.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 2× (recipe serves 6), on two sheet pans

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Boil 10 min, air-dry 10 min, roast at 450°F with fan for 20 + 20 min, melted butter to finish

lines.label: Note
lines.text: Serve straight away. Crowding the pan makes them soggy.

recipe.title: Crispy roasted potatoes

steps.t: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. For extra crunch, add {soda} baking soda.

steps: Boil {potatoes} halved potatoes about 10 minutes, until nearly tender.
Drain and leave them to air-dry in the colander for 10 minutes. Shake them once at the 5-minute mark to rough up the edges.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 450°F with fan, or 475°F without.
Spread the potatoes on two parchment-lined sheet pans about an inch apart. Toss with {oil} olive oil, {gp} garlic powder, {op} onion powder, {paprika} paprika, and salt and pepper.

steps: Roast 20 minutes.

steps.t: Flip and rearrange the potatoes, then roast 20 minutes more, until golden brown.
Drizzle with {butter} melted butter and serve straight away.

notes: Two pans because crowding steams them. Swap the pans between racks when you flip.
To hold them, skip the butter and keep them in a 200°F oven for up to an hour.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: Two separate batches, 28–32 rolls (Sally advises against doubling)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: 350°F for 20–25 min on a lower rack

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Bake the day before, or shape and refrigerate overnight, or freeze.

recipe.title: Soft dinner rolls
recipe.servings: Makes 14–16 rolls per batch. Make two batches.
recipe.time: Prep 25 min · rising about 3 hr · bake 22 min

steps.t: Whisk {milk} warm milk, {yeast} instant yeast and {sugar:1 tbsp} sugar together. Let stand 5 minutes.

steps: Add {sugar:rest} sugar, {egg} egg, {butter} softened butter, {salt} salt and {flour:1 cup} flour. Mix on low speed.
Add {flour:rest} flour and mix on medium until the dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl. Only if it is too sticky, add more flour a tablespoon at a time.
Knead 5 minutes by mixer or by hand, until soft and slightly tacky. A poke should spring back slowly.
Put the dough in a greased bowl, turn it to coat, cover and let it rise 1 to 2 hours, until doubled.
Grease a 9×13-inch pan.
Punch down the dough. Divide it into 14 to 16 pieces and shape each into a smooth ball. Arrange them in the pan.
Cover and let rise about 1 hour, until puffy.
Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in a lower position.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until golden, turning the pan halfway. Tent with foil if the tops brown too fast.
Optional: brush with {butter2} melted butter mixed with {honey} honey. Cool, then cover tightly.

steps.t: Warm the rolls in the air fryer on low for a few minutes, checking often. Or reheat covered at 300°F for about 10 minutes.

notes: Amounts are for one batch. Sally advises against doubling, so make the batch twice.
Baked rolls keep 2–3 days covered at room temperature, or freeze for 3 months.
Overnight option: refrigerate the shaped rolls up to 15 hours, then let them rise 1–2 hours on the counter before baking.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 3 lb for 10

lines.label: Ingredients
lines.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp butter, 4 garlic cloves thinly sliced, zest and juice of 1 lemon, salt and pepper

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Blanch 2–3 min the day before, then sauté in two batches for 4–5 min just before serving. Garlic goes in for the last minute so it does not burn.

recipe.title: Garlic lemon green beans
recipe.time: Blanch 5 min the day before · sauté 10 min

ingredients.name: salt and pepper
ingredients.unmeasured: to taste, plus salt for the water

steps.t: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and fill a big bowl with ice water.

steps: Boil {beans} green beans for 2 to 3 minutes, until bright green. Drain and plunge them into the ice water.
Dry well and refrigerate in a towel-lined container.

steps.t: Heat {oil:1/2} olive oil and {butter:1/2} butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the beans and sauté 4 to 5 minutes, until hot and lightly blistered.

steps: For the last minute, add {garlic:1/2} sliced garlic cloves. Move to a serving dish.
Repeat with {oil:rest} olive oil, {butter:rest} butter, the rest of the beans and {garlic:rest} garlic cloves.
Finish with the zest of {lemon} lemon, a squeeze of its juice, and salt and pepper.
notes: Garlic goes in last so it doesn't burn.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 3 lb medium carrots (about 20) for 10

lines.label: Ingredients
lines.text: 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp salt, pepper. Glaze: 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp chopped fresh thyme.

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Roast whole at 425°F for 25–30 min at midday, chill, then glaze and reheat uncovered at 350°F for about 20 min with the casseroles.

recipe.title: Honey-thyme roasted whole carrots
recipe.time: Roast 30 min at midday · glaze and reheat 20 min

ingredients.name: medium carrots
ingredients.note: about 20, peeled, tops trimmed, left whole

steps.t: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.

steps: Toss {carrots} carrots with {oil} olive oil, {salt} salt and some pepper.
Spread them in one layer with space between them.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until browned and just tender with a little bite left. They finish cooking in the reheat.

steps.t: Cool 30 minutes, cover and refrigerate.
Melt {butter} butter with {honey} honey and {thyme} thyme. Toss with the carrots on their pan.

steps: Reheat uncovered at 350°F for about 20 minutes. Short on oven room? Use the air fryer at 350°F for 6 to 8 minutes.
notes: Pick slim carrots of a similar size so they cook evenly.

lines.label: Size
lines.text: One batch (recipe serves 10)

lines.label: Method
lines.text: Simmer cranberries with sugar and water about 15 min, finish with orange zest, cinnamon and nutmeg. Chill 30–45 min.

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Up to 2 days ahead (keeps 7 days in the fridge, or freezes for 3 months).

recipe.title: Cranberry sauce
recipe.time: Prep 5 min · cook 20 min · chill 45 min

steps.t: In a high-sided medium pot, bring {water} water and {sugar} sugar to a full boil.

steps: Add {cranberries} cranberries and bring back to a boil, until they start to pop.
Cover and simmer about 15 minutes, until very thick. Add a splash of water if the pot looks dry.
Off the heat, stir in {cinnamon} cinnamon, {nutmeg} nutmeg and the zest of {orange} orange, pressing the berries to break them up.
Move to a container and refrigerate until cold, at least 30 to 45 minutes.
notes: Keeps 7 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. It thickens and tastes better cold.

menu.name: Spinach salad with pears and pecans

lines.label: Size
lines.text: 15 oz baby spinach for 10

lines.label: Ingredients
lines.text: 2 ripe pears, 1 cup pomegranate seeds, 1 cup toasted pecans, 3 oz shaved Parmesan

lines.label: Dressing
lines.text: Apple cider vinaigrette: ½ cup olive oil, ¼ cup cider vinegar, 1 tbsp each Dijon and maple syrup, 1 small shallot, salt and pepper

lines.label: Make ahead
lines.text: Dressing and pecans the day before. No cooking on the day, just slice the pears and toss at 5:45.

recipe.title: Spinach salad with pears and pecans
recipe.time: Dressing 5 min the day before · assemble 10 min

steps.t: Shake {oil} olive oil, {vinegar} apple cider vinegar, {dijon} Dijon, {maple} maple syrup, {shallot} minced shallot, {salt} salt and some pepper in a jar. Refrigerate.

steps: Toast {pecans} pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring. Cool, then store airtight.

steps.t: Take the dressing out of the fridge so it loosens, and shake it.
Thinly slice {pears} pears. Do it now, not earlier, so they don't brown.

steps: Toss {spinach} baby spinach with about two-thirds of the dressing.
Top with the pears, {pom} pomegranate seeds, the pecans and {parm} Parmesan shaved with a vegetable peeler. Serve the rest of the dressing on the side.
notes: No cooking on the day, so this is a good job for a helper.

open.note: You asked to be reminded. It affects the potatoes (450°F with fan, 475°F without).

open.text: Allergies or dietary needs among the 10 guests
open.note: The stuffing has pork sausage, and the turkey is wrapped in bacon. Does anyone avoid meat or pork?

open.text: Fresh or frozen turkey, and where you'll get it

open.note: Flipping and carving the turkey are the two jobs worth assigning. Also table, drinks and the salad.

open.text: Rolls: bake the day before, or fresh on the day?
open.note: The plan bakes them the day before to keep the oven free on the day.

open.text: Something for guests to nibble while the turkey rests (optional)

callouts.title: If the turkey is late.
callouts.text: Leave it in until it reads 165°F. Skip the oven reheat, warm the stuffing, yams and carrots in the microwave in portions, and put the potatoes in once the turkey is out.

callouts.title: For a lighter day.
callouts.text: Bake the stuffing, yams and carrots on D−1 and reheat them from the fridge on the day.
